text:
amanda: Heads-up — Support routed an escalation that mixes a customer-facing API error (5xx spikes), billing anomalies, and a pen-test finding around key metadata exposure. Ticket: https://redwood.support/8872 :white_flag:
raj: can you paste the stacktrace / CloudTrail slices? need repro steps to reproduce the 500s and the alleged key metadata leak.
amanda: summary from support:
- Customers saw intermittent 502/504s on /v1/generate between 02:15–03:40 UTC yesterday (approx 1.8% of requests)
- Billing spike correlated with retry storms for affected tenants
- Pen test report says KMS aliases can be enumerated via error differences when calling our presign endpoint (low-traffic repro attached by pen team)
joel: adding the quick logs I grabbed from gateway logs (sanitized):
```
502 GET /v1/generate 200ms - upstream timeout
504 POST /v1/presign 10ms - handshake failed: key-not-found
200 POST /v1/presign 12ms - ok
```
looks like presign timing differs between missing vs present keys.
sylvia: do we have the pen-test repro steps? did they use the API key of a customer? is this auth-scoped or an info-leak from our control plane?
amanda: pen team attached curl script and CloudTrail query. repro steps (from their report):
1) enumerate aliases by probing /v1/presign with random alias names and watch error body/time differences
2) escalate by correlating alias names to customer metadata in our billing db
I ran a quick retest in staging and could reproduce similar timing delta (~8–15ms).
sara: support-bot posted the customer ticket and billing trace: https://redwood.support/8872/trace — shows a retry backoff loop, client retried on 502 which blew up token usage.
incident-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT: spike_detected /v1/generate 02:15–03:40 UTC (p95 latency 420ms -> 900ms). Correlation: presign 404/timeout pattern flagged.
raj: ok action items: (1) confirm whether presign leaks alias existence to unauthenticated callers, (2) collect CloudTrail for KMS calls + presign logs, (3) confirm billing attribution per tenant, (4) decide severity (P1/P2). I'll take 1+2.
joel: pasted the CloudTrail query I used:
```
fields @timestamp, eventName, requestParameters
| filter eventSource = "kms.amazonaws.com" and eventName like "*Decrypt*" or eventName like "Generate*"
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 50
```
gives us KMS invocations around the same window.
sylvia: severity debate — pen team labeled as "medium" but support impact + billing makes this potentially P1 because it affected customer-facing latency and costs. preferences? :thinking_face: 
amanda: customer SLA impact + billing hit pushes me to P1. but we'd prefer to avoid over-escalating if it's an info-leak with low exploitability. request: raj, can you produce a minimal repro showing alias-enumeration WITHOUT any privileged keys? that's critical for severity.
raj: working on that now, will try unauthenticated and just our public presign endpoint. ETA 60m.
sara: flagged for customer comms — tentative message: "We're investigating an intermittent error pattern affecting presign and generation endpoints and its billing impact. We're working with engineering and security; we'll follow up in 4 hours with initial findings." ok?
joel: patch suggestion for mitigation (short term): normalize presign error responses and add constant-time error path to avoid timing differences. also rate-limit presign per origin to dampen enumeration.
sylvia: long-term: review KMS usage patterns, avoid leaking alias names in error messages, use aggregated error metrics for internal troubleshooting instead of returning fine-grained errors to callers. also evaluate rotating any keys that may be enumerated.
amanda: agreed. raj — after you have repro, please run a controlled retest and capture pcap/latency histograms and post the sanitized script. we'll want the pen team to validate retest results. set up a canary patch in staging to normalize responses.
raj: update — minimal repro using curl + random alias shows consistent 12ms delta between not-found vs success. attaching sanitized curl in thread (posted to internal gist).
incident-bot: NOTE: Evidence uploaded to incident vault at https://vault.internal/evidence/esc-2061234567 (access: eng-security).
sylvia: based on repro, severity: P1 -> we need immediate mitigations (normalize errors + short-term rate limiting) and a follow-up key rotation plan for exposed aliases. I'll open a remediation ticket and add owners.
amanda: I'll coordinate customer comms and billing credits evaluation with support. assigning remediation owners: raj (repro + patches), joel (logging + CloudTrail aggregation), sylvia (severity + KMS policy review), sara (customer comms).
support-bot: created remediation ticket #MS-4432 and linked support ticket 8872.
raj: starting a staging PR to normalize presign responses now. will request quick review from eng-runtime.
amanda: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread and ping me for any roadblocks. :thumbsup:
